title: rover_msgs Software Requirements Specification
scope: rover_msgs defines the custom ROS 2 messages and services of the Rover A1 stack. The safety-relevant contracts are SafetyStatus (plant state of the E-Stop chain, the only message that may permit motion), SafetyCommandEcho (read-backs of software-driven safety coils, inhibit-only), AuxIoState (non-safety PLC IO), RoverDriverState and its nested DriverStateNamed / DriverState / FaultFlag / RuntimeError (motor driver health), RcLinkStatus (RC link quality), ChargingStatus and the LED animation catalogue. Safety commands are deliberately not messages: they are std_srvs/Trigger services served by rover_hardware_interface.

requirements.text: The rover_msgs shall define rover_msgs/SafetyStatus with fields std_msgs/Header header, builtin_interfaces/Time io_sample_time, bool hw_e_stop_user_button, bool motor_contactor_engaged, bool latch_active, uint8 latch_cause and bool link_healthy.
requirements.rationale: SYS-SR-023 requires the HW and SW E-Stop state on a ROS topic; this is the plant-state half of the old GpioState and the only safety message consumers may gate motion on.
requirements.acceptance: ros2 interface show rover_msgs/msg/SafetyStatus lists exactly these fields and types; publisher and subscriber tests compile and exchange the message.

requirements.text: The rover_msgs shall document in SafetyStatus that hw_e_stop_user_button true means pressed, motor_contactor_engaged true means contacts closed (drive live), latch_active true means the E-Stop latch holds a stop, and link_healthy false means the other fields are last-known-good values that must not be trusted.
requirements.rationale: Unambiguous field semantics (including the inverted sense of motor_contactor_engaged) prevent consumers from gating on the wrong polarity (SYS-SR-023, SYS-SR-022).
requirements.acceptance: Each of the four fields carries a comment stating its true/false meaning as above.

requirements.text: The rover_msgs shall define SafetyStatus.io_sample_time as the time the safety PLC was polled, distinct from header.stamp (the publish time), for use by consumer staleness checks.
requirements.rationale: Staleness must measure data age, not transport age (SYS-SR-023 latency, SYS-SR-022).
requirements.acceptance: Field present and documented; a published sample has io_sample_time <= header.stamp.

requirements.text: The rover_msgs shall define the SafetyStatus latch_cause constants LATCH_CAUSE_UNKNOWN = 0, LATCH_CAUSE_SW_USER_BUTTON = 1, LATCH_CAUSE_SW_MOTOR_DRIVER_FAULT = 2, LATCH_CAUSE_CPU_WATCHDOG = 3 and LATCH_CAUSE_HW_USER_BUTTON = 4.
requirements.rationale: Lets consumers and logs report why the rover stopped once the PLC exposes the trip source (SYS-SR-023, SYS-SR-022).
requirements.acceptance: ros2 interface show lists the five constants with these values.
requirements.comments: Contract defined, but the publisher never sets the field, so it is always LATCH_CAUSE_UNKNOWN (see rover_hardware_interface SWRS, latch_cause requirement).

requirements.text: The rover_msgs shall define rover_msgs/SafetyCommandEcho (header, io_sample_time, sw_e_stop_user_button, sw_e_stop_motor_driver_fault, sw_e_stop_latch_reset, cpu_wdg_heartbeat) and document that its fields may be used only to inhibit motion, never to permit it, and that cpu_wdg_heartbeat and sw_e_stop_latch_reset carry no stop state.
requirements.rationale: Separating command echoes from plant state is what stops a consumer from treating "we asked for a stop" as evidence the hardware stopped (SAFETY_CHAIN.md §4); gating on the heartbeat once made a motion lock oscillate.
requirements.acceptance: ros2 interface show lists the six fields; the header comment states the inhibit-only rule; the heartbeat and latch-reset comments state that neither level is a stop condition.
requirements.comments: Doc drift: the sw_e_stop_latch_reset comment (line 30) says the pulse is driven "true then immediately false"; the publisher now holds it for safety_latch_reset_pulse_ms (100 ms), so a 10 Hz poll may observe true.

requirements.text: The rover_msgs shall not define any message type that carries a safety command (E-Stop set, E-Stop reset or latch reset).
requirements.rationale: A safety command needs an acknowledgement and must never be replayed to a late joiner, so it is a service (std_srvs/Trigger) and not a topic (SYS-SR-007, SAFETY_CHAIN.md §4).
requirements.acceptance: No .msg in rover_msgs/msg contains an E-Stop set/reset or latch-reset command field; there is no GpioControl message.
requirements.comments: Design constraint verified by inspection only.

requirements.text: The rover_msgs shall define rover_msgs/AuxIoState with header, io_sample_time, bool[6] inputs (PLC DIO06..DIO11), bool[6] outputs (read-back of DIO00..DIO05) and link_healthy, documented as outside the safety chain.
requirements.rationale: General-purpose PLC IO must be available without anyone gating motion on it.
requirements.acceptance: ros2 interface show lists the fixed-size arrays of 6; rover_hardware_interface static_asserts the array sizes against its pin counts.
requirements.derived_rationale: Non-safety auxiliary interface; no SYS-SR parent.

requirements.text: The rover_msgs shall define rover_msgs/RoverDriverState (header, DriverStateNamed[] driver_states, bool error) whose DriverState carries current, temperature, FaultFlag (emergency_stop, motor_setup_fault), RuntimeError (safety_stop_active), motor_states_data_timed_out, driver_state_data_timed_out, comm_error and heartbeat_timeout.
requirements.acceptance: ros2 interface show rover_msgs/msg/RoverDriverState expands to these nested fields; the driver-state publisher test receives a populated message.
requirements.comments: Doc drift: DriverStateNamed name constants are "default"/"front"/"rear", but the publisher uses "front_left"/"front_right"/"rear_left"/"rear_right" (rover_hardware_interface/include/rover_hardware_interface/domain/driver.hpp:50-63). heartbeat_timeout is never set by any publisher.

requirements.text: The rover_msgs shall define rover_msgs/RcLinkStatus carrying the CRSF LINK_STATISTICS uplink RSSI (both antennas), uplink_link_quality (0-100 %), uplink SNR, active antenna, rf_mode, uplink TX power and the downlink RSSI, link quality and SNR.
requirements.rationale: Uplink link quality is what gates teleop, i.e. the observable for SYS-SR-012 loss of the operator link on the RC path.
requirements.acceptance: ros2 interface show lists the fields; the CRSF conversion unit test fills them from a LINK_STATISTICS frame.

requirements.text: The rover_msgs shall define rover_msgs/LedAnimation animation ids covering every SYS-SR-010 system state, including a Boot state.
requirements.rationale: SYS-SR-009 requires a defined state-to-LED mapping for each SYS-SR-010 state (Boot, Idle, Teleoperation, Autonomous, Emergency Stop, Fault, Low Battery).
requirements.acceptance: For each SYS-SR-010 state there is a named LedAnimation constant; the mapping table is documented.
requirements.comments: Existing ids plausibly cover Idle (READY), Teleoperation (MANUAL_ACTION), Autonomous (AUTONOMOUS_READY / AUTONOMOUS_ACTION), Emergency Stop (E_STOP), Fault (ERROR) and Low Battery (LOW_BATTERY); there is no Boot id. The state-to-id mapping is an interpretation (TBC) and is not documented in rover_msgs. rover_safety/test/unit/test_led_animation_policy.cpp covers the current policy in rover_safety.

requirements.text: The rover_msgs shall define a system-state message whose state constants enumerate at least Boot, Idle, Teleoperation, Autonomous, Emergency Stop, Fault and Low Battery.
requirements.rationale: SYS-SR-010 requires a defined system state machine whose transitions can be observed; no rover_msgs type carries it.
requirements.acceptance: ros2 interface show on the new message lists the seven state constants.
requirements.comments: SystemStatus carries only CPU / RAM / disk telemetry. MissionState and LocalizationState cover sub-states of navigation only.

requirements.text: The rover_msgs shall generate all messages and services with rosidl_generate_interfaces depending only on builtin_interfaces, geometry_msgs and std_msgs, and export rosidl_default_runtime.
requirements.rationale: Keeps the interface package light so every node can depend on it (SYS-SR-020 ROS 2 based software).
requirements.acceptance: colcon build --packages-select rover_msgs succeeds and ros2 interface list | grep rover_msgs lists every .msg and .srv in the package.
requirements.comments: CMakeLists.txt finds builtin_interfaces twice (lines 9 and 11); harmless. No tests in rover_msgs itself.
